questions.question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct?

8 and 2
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

By option Method:

**Option 1 : exchange **8 and 2 in 7 ÷ 2 – 8 × 4 + 1 = 0

⇒ **7 ÷ 8** – **2 × 4** + 1 = 0

⇒ 0.87 - 8 + 1 =0

⇒ -6.125 ≠ 0

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 2 : exchange **8 and 2 in 2 × 4 – 8 + 5 ÷ 1 = 50

⇒ **8 × 4** – 2 + **5 ÷ 1** = 50 

⇒ 32 - 2 + 5 = 50

⇒ 35 ≠ 50

This is not correct the equation.

**Option 3 : exchange **8 and 2 in 8 × 4 + 6 – 2 ÷ 1 = 6

⇒ **2 × 4** + 6 – **8 ÷ 1 **= 6

⇒ 8 +6 -8 = 6

⇒ 6 = 6

This is correct the equation.

**Option 4 : exchange **8 and 2 in 8 × 4 – 9 ÷ 3 + 2 = 35

⇒ **2 × 4** – **9 ÷ 3** + 8 = 35

⇒ 8 - 3 + 8 = 35

⇒ 13 ≠ 35

This is not correct the equation.

Hence, **'Option 3'** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All R are H.

II. Some T are R.

**Conclusion:**

I. All H are R.

II. All T are H.

III. No R is T.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
Statements:
I. All R are H.
II. Some T are R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96af13b97fd1b5030f9735a95953b8a912800880c5c48781af2d5f8e93438f1c.png] 
Conclusions:
I. All H are R → Does not follow → Since 'All R are H' that means All H are R is a possibility not necessity so conclusion does not follow
II. All T are H → Does not follow → Since 'All R are H' & Some T are R. that also means 'All T are H' is a possibility not necessity so conclusion does not follow
III. No R is T → Does not follow → Since 'Some T are R'. that also means Some part of R lies in T so conclusion does not follow.

Hence, **Neither conclusion follows.**

questions.question: If A + B means that A is the father of B, A ÷ B means that A is the mother of B, A × B means that A is the brother of B then which of the following expression shows that Q is the sister of P?
questions.solution:

**Given:**

 
 

 **Code** 
 **Meaning**
 
 

 A + B
 A is the father of B
 
 

 A ÷ B
 A is the mother of B
 
 

 A × B
 A is the brother of B
 
 

**Given expression:**

Q is the sister of P

**Option 1 : **P × Q + R

P × Q means that P is the brother of Q

Q + R means that Q is the father of R

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfc81aac6f5016c5aad702af60eefedc3b31b9509884958e2b4f8de42a523a06.png] 

Here, Q is brother of P.

Option 2 : P + R × Q

P + R means that P is the father of R

R × Q means that R is the brother of Q

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ad83306fa4cec19d74dc22b3001ac8524e949b16be61514a1acf87cf0ff5d39.png] 

Here gender of Q Unknown.

Option 3 : P × Q ÷ R

P × Q means that P is the brother of Q

Q ÷ R means that Q is the mother of R

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/129ab2d510a14c9f03ea35cda2ccf1a82e6ce81028d22f23d888df2ca069bb35.png] 

Here, Q is the sister of P. So it will be answer.

Option 4 : Q × P ÷ R

Q × P means that Q is the brother of P

P ÷ R means that P is the mother of R

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e771096a77c75221837123699ebec49b02952d8cc0ac8368ceb454db6e1391.png] 

Here, Q is the brother P.

Hence, **'Option 3'** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct?

5 and 9
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

**1) **9 – 5 × 4 + 6 ÷ 3 = 30

After interchanging the numbers 5 and 9, we get

5 – 9 × 4 + 6 ÷ 3 = 30

Applying the BODMAS Rule, we get

5 – 9 × 4 + 2 = 30

⇒ 5 – 36 + 2 = 30

⇒ 7 - 36 = 30

⇒ - 29 ≠ 30

The given equation is incorrect.

**2) **9 × 3 + 5 ÷ 1 – 6 = 20

After interchanging the numbers 5 and 9, we get

5 × 3 + 9 ÷ 1 – 6 = 20

Applying the BODMAS Rule, we get

5 × 3 + 9 – 6 = 20

⇒ 15 + 9 - 6 = 20

⇒ 24 - 6 = 20

⇒ 18 ≠ 20

The given equation is incorrect.

**3)** 7 × 9 + 5 – 8 ÷ 4 = 40

After interchanging the numbers 5 and 9, we get

7 × 5 + 9 – 8 ÷ 4 = 40

Applying the BODMAS Rule, we get

7 × 5 + 9 – 2= 40

⇒ 35 + 9 - 2 = 40

⇒ 44 - 2 = 40

⇒ 42 ≠ 40

The given equation is incorrect.

**4)** 9 × 4 + 5 – 8 ÷ 2 = 25

After interchanging the numbers 5 and 9, we get

5 × 4 + 9 – 8 ÷ 2 = 25

Applying the BODMAS Rule, we get

5 × 4 + 9 – 4 = 25

⇒ 20 + 9 – 4 = 25

⇒ 29 - 4 = 25

⇒ 25 = 25

The given equation is correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **'****9 × 4 + 5 – 8 ÷ 2 = 25'**.

questions.question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some apples are fruits.

All fruits are vegetables.

No vegetable is healthy.

**Conclusions:**

I- No apple is healthy.

II- No healthy is vegetable.

III- Some vegetables are apples.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:
Some apples are fruits.
All fruits are vegetables.
No vegetable is healthy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c266c84ec41f55797f50eca8cc64736684786fa956f650ed79362ca7568532f.png] 

Conclusions:
I- No apple is healthy → False (No direct relationship given between apple and healthy, so it may be possible but not defined)
II- No healthy is vegetable → True (It is given that no vegetable is healthy, so no healthy is vegetable)
III- Some vegetables are apples → True (It is given that some apples are fruits and all fruits are vegetables, so some vegetables are apples)

Hence, **"Only conclusions II and III follow"**.
